Airtales

By: Hein Kaiser | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
we question whether our skies are as safe as we are made to believe by our regulator, the Civil Aviation Authority

Unique Selling Point:
Aviation fascinates audience, and this story introduces an element of significant tension as it will show the danger of corruption or sweeping investigations under the carpet can have devastating consequences. What are the dangers that lurk beneath the surface of shiny aircraft that fly us from A to B?

Further information:
Are we safe when we fly? We look at 3 incidents that make us wonder whether we are as safe in the skies as we are led to believe.

Firstly we look at training - and examine the case of Sim Aero, who seem to be up to dirty tricks in the industry in order to make more money. They have actively tried to put competitors out of business.

But in doing so, our baddie Keith (the manager at Sim Aero) is about to be arrested for various nasty activities, including sexual harassment. But we look at his qualifications - he claims to be an examiner that can train and pass out pilots. But he is not. We have found at least one pilot that was signed out, illegally, by Keith and whose license leap frogged from a private license to piloting a twin engine passenger jet without any learning in between. And flying a commercial jet means this unqualified pilot is responsible for our lives.

We confront Keith and the CAA inspector that we have on record (audio and affidavit from an investigator) that has taken bribes from Keith to destroy a competitor.

The competitor, Ricky Smit from Sky Voyage, will narrate this ordeal for us.

Then there is the curious case of SAA’s successful dodging of two incident investigations.

We also look at 3 SAA incidents in the past 2 years that were never investigated. - the SAA Alpha Floor and noise abatement charges in Belgium. The crew who operated the flights did not complete their update training, it was waivered by the CAA in order to operate the flight- and the consequences could have been a crash over Joburg (Alpha Floor) It was the same commander in charge on both legs and there has never been an investigation into either incidents, as required by law, nor has SAA ever really answered the questions. Meanwhile, the commander was promoted to head of training.

Meanwhile the same captain operated a flight on contaminated fuel from Ghana to Johannesburg - with more potential hazard for passengers. There were no consequences to either incident, it seems. And no investigation with an outcome by the CAA despite it being a dangerous and reportable event.

ZA CARS - Joy did an insert, but we focus on the recent developments where the Ethiopian Accident Bureau investigation pointe to the CCA's complete lack of maintenance of the aircraft, the accident report said it was not airworthy, and how the Minister has now invalidated the enquiry.

Reports swept under the carpet and brown envelopes, is this what our skies look like?

There are some other operators who have an office, and not much else, yet they seem to be above the law.

Malik of Cobra Air who has an AOC (Air Operator Certificate) but no aircraft - how does he pass inspections and how does he, along with FlyFofa, who are in the same position, manage to hang onto certification when they have nothing to certify?

In addition, Keith from Sim Aero is about to be arrested on several charges. We will be there for the arrest.

Planned confrontations:

1. Vox Pops (Malik, FlyFofa)
2. Keith at SIm Aero and his boss, Eric Renau
3. CAA
4. CAA official taking bribes (Jason Maistry)
5. SAA

Interviews
1. Ricky
2. Aviation Expert
3. Airlines who are compliant (for balance)

AIRTALES SCRIPT
When a South African Airways Airbus A340-600 landed in Johannesburg from Accra, Ghana on 15 April last year, all was not as it seemed. During the flight, the plane’s engines started surging – an unusual occurrence for any aircraft as it may suggest contaminated fuel and demands urgent action from the flight crew. Alarmingly, though, the flight’s commander chose to continue flying back to O.R. Tambo International Airport… It was the third in a series of four recent incidents involving SAA. But, while other airlines have been grounded over safety concerns, the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) - mandated with regulating our airspace - has taken no action against the national carrier. Our probe uncovers evidence that all is not well at the CAA, undermining our country’s reputation for sterling air safety.


Clip and Code
Script
1


Setting foot on a plane, means putting your life in the hands of other PEOPLE… pilots, engineers, air traffic controllers and cabin crew…
TO DATE South Africa had a reputation for safe air travel…our airspace tightly regulated…thanks to the Civil Aviation Authority.
The CAA upholds a vast web of international laws and standards…
…but could a number of incidents and the organisation’s own conduct over the last two years…raise questions over air safety?
2
Mike “Allen”
Cam 1
C080
MIKE: [00:01:58] I think the CAA has become a political animal now. So consequently, as I say, it hears and it's guided by its political masters rather than its own, skill and the job it should be doing.
3


The CAA has rarely hesitated to act where it deemed safety was at stake. Cemair… Kulula… British Airways… and the maintenance company Lufthansa Technik …ALL GROUNDED in the last three years.
4
Links 0807
LINK: [17:38:31] South Africa's civil aviation authority flexes its muscles from time to time. But it seems at others, it turns a blind eye… are some airlines more equal than others?
5


Four incidents since 2021 might mean little in isolation.. but together…do they spell a dire warning?
February 2021 - the national carrier South African Airways has a potentially disastrous safety incident on what we’ll call the BRUSSELS flight…
April 2022 - a whistleblower leaks information that passengers were flown from Accra, Ghana to Joburg… in a plane with contaminated fuel..
and November 2022…an SAA plane bumper-bashes a Safair jet on the OR TAMBO airport apron.
6
Guy Leitch Day 1 Cam 1
0749
Guy Leitch is an aviation analyst and the editor of SA FLYER MAGAZINE
UPSOUND: GUY [00:07:47] safety is a non-negotiable. Safety has to be taken for granted by the passengers.
7


Flying safely is all about preparation…about operating manuals and checklists and rigorous annual refresher training for the crew. Skipping a step …can be a problem.
In February 2021 the government sent an SAA Airbus A340 600 to Belgium to collect Covid vaccines.
SAA was in business rescue… air travel was in lockdown…the pilots needed refresher training.
The CAA stopped SAA TWICE when not all the training was in place…but then, in an unusual move.. it waived some training requirements.






9
Colin Jordaan
E.N-20230129_0001


For former SAA Pilot Colin Jordaan who headed up the CAA a decade ago the decision raised red flags.
[00:08:12] it's difficult to understand what evidence could have been presented by the operator by, say, in order for this exemption to be granted. I certainly can't think of anything.
10


Without refresher training, pilots may not know that
the Airbus A340 600 has a known computer glitch that is considered minor… if you know about it.
If you don’t, it could kill you.
On startup the plane’s computer SOMETIMES deducts around 80 tons from the weight data that the pilots capture manually… sudden weight loss impacts the plane’s ability to fly.
11
Mike
0807
Allen, not his real name, is a retired SAA pilot, who flew the A340-600 for a decade.
[00:04:49] it's core to the whole aspect of a safe flight is knowing exactly how heavy your aircraft is….You're flying an aircraft that weighs 340 tons with 300 people or so. So you basically need to have those those factors and those figures are crucial and critical.
12


Several training documents and a cockpit checklist warn pilots about the glitch…In a report, SAA said those were not present on the Brussels flight which instead used an Airbus checklist that excluded the glitch.
13
COLIN JORDAAN
E.N-20230129_0001


[00:16:08] I flew Airbus A340 600 from their inception. And that checklist was introduced exactly because this problem had occurred.
15


Moments into the flight, warnings sounded…the plane was about to stall..

Luckily the Airbus has a failsafe called the Alpha Floor system…
16
Mike “Allen”
0807
MIKE UPSOUND You could equate it almost to an ABS type of system on a motor car. It's to protect the aircraft from stalling.
17


The Alpha Floor saved the day… and potentially the lives of thousands of people on the ground.


Had the CAA not waived the training requirement, it’s likely all this would have been avoided.
18



The plane landed in Brussels, loaded the vaccines and a day later headed off home. The pilots didn't tell anyone about the incident but the plane is designed to send a message to Airbus and engine manufacturer Rolls Royce.

Incidents like this must be reported to the CAA within 72 hours.

In fear of a near stall happening again, the pilots took off from on the return flight at a higher speed than European Union regulations allow - knowingly breaking an important law.
19
Mike Allen
[00:16:25] the manually applied maximum thrust, which promptly had a aircraft behaving like a raging bull, if you like, and heading for the heavens at high speed.
20


Neither the pilots nor SAA said anything until a whistleblower leaked the information.
21
Link
0810
[17:47:09] SAA hasn't said much about the events which have unfolded, and they wouldn't speak to us saying they didn't want to get involved in a smear campaign. But it is unfair to expect transparency?
22
CAA ROR
SAA presented a confidential incident report in Parliament a few weeks ago.
The airline said.. the checklists that show the glitch have been put back..
23


PAUSE AND TRANSITION TO RICKY
But what the report didn’t say was that refresher training for pilots and crew could have prevented the whole debacle.
24


Meanwhile, within months of the Brussels flight, a local flight school owner would butt heads with the CAA in an incident which may at first seem like a personal spat. But, in the context of safety… it raises serious questions.
Flight schools provide ongoing pilot training which the CAA licences and oversees.
25
Colin Jordaan
E.N-20230129_0001


UPSOUND COLIN JORDAAN [00:09:11] Over the years, there have been a lot of instances where. Flying schools have used the CAA inspectors to achieve their own particular goals.
28


UPSOUND RICKIE [14:32:20] It's hugely competitive. It's very competitive. It's sometimes very cutthroat as well.
29


When Rickie Smit took over the reins at Sky Voyage in 2021 she had to apply for a new license…
Owning a business was a big moment in her life…but on the sidelines, a competitor was plotting...
30


LINK It all started right here, at Denel’s Kempton Park Campus at the back of OR Tambo International Airport. This is where there is a simulator that Ricky uses.
31


… and when Ricky got a call from a prospective new client, she made a booking with THAT service provider.
32



But the call had come from a former client of a company called SimAero…
which also has offices in the Denel complex
33


RICKY INTERVIEW [14:39:02] when I made a booking for a client to do training on. And on a simulator, not belonging to SimAero. I was called and told by SimAero staff that I'm stealing their clients.
34


DEREK [14:39:19] Were you? [14:39:19][0.3]
35


RICKY: [14:39:20] Absolutely not. There's no way I would steal anybody's clients
36


Calls and threats escalated -including from SimAero manager, Keith Roseveare…
37


RICKY: [14:41:16] I was bombarded with threats, but it all came through calls that I received. It was things like, if you don't give up the simulation to Simaero, you will be destroyed. I will make sure that you'll never operate again. We will have you shut down. We will make sure your operation will be completely demolished. There will be hell to pay
38


It turns out that SimAero tried to discredit her in any way possible.

Eventually Roseveare reported Ricky for illegal training. His evidence: mock up training documents she used in preparation for a CAA audit that would have earned Sky Voyage its license.




39


Then Rickie got a call from a CAA Inspector who told her he was putting her licensing process on ice.
But why would a company be shut down for dummy documents? Or was something else at play?
PAUSE FOR DRAMA

Coming up: From sweeping incidents under the carpet.. to shutting down industry entrepreneurs.. is this the role South Africans expect the CAA to play?

ADBREAK



40


PART 2 INTRO

The safety of our airspace depends on the Civil Aviation Authority policing the industry without fear or favour..
In part two we confront the inspector accused of shutting down a flight school at the behest of a competitor … and probe the infamous contaminated fuel flight.
41


TRANSITION BACK TO RICKY
42


Rickie Smit says a competitor threatened her for months, claiming a SimAero employee once relayed a disturbing message from his manager, Keith Roseveare - which Roseveare later denied.
43
Day 2 Cam 1
P1644645


RICKY : [14:42:06] He'll start by shooting my feet off and in my hands. And the only hell squeeze every blood cell out of my body until I'm left for dead.
44




45


Then, the CAA inspector Rickie relied on to help her through the trainer licensing process turned against her.
45


RICKY: I got a call from Jason Maestri And he told me that. He's calling me to tell me that he's cancelling the audit that was set for the next day to start. And the reason is that I acted fraudulently. I did illegal training.
46


Maistry shut Sky Voyage down…
The CAA could never produce evidence of wrongdoing against Rickie - its own legal department exonerated her and told Maistry to issue her licence.
But Maistry simply ignored the instruction.
49


DEREK: [15:00:10] Are you saying that the CAA was weaponised by a competitor?
50


RICKY: [15:00:15] Yes, they used Jason to weaponize themselves to achieve a goal so that they can take out another competitor out of the market
51

Keith Roseveare and Sim Aero did not want to talk to us… his attorneys sent court documents showing that he’s suing Ricky for defamation.
The CAA wouldn’t be drawn on Rickie - saying in writing they have no knowledge of Rickie’s plight and asking us to give them our information.
So we went straight to the source.
52
Day 2 Cam 1
P1644661


[16:38:11] is this Jason Maistry?
JASON: YES
DEREK: This is Derek from Carte Blanche.
Jason Maistry talked in circles for a long time, trying to avoid speaking about Keith Roseveare. Eventually, he slipped up.
54


Jason Call

[16:55:40] It came from the .. what is now opposition right, which was obviously from Keith. And because they had valid, valid evidence from the quality point of view or the quality management point of view. They found that, you know, a certain person was operating without a valid license.
[16:56:08] But, Jason, this is what I've been asking you. And now you admitting that Keith Roseveare influenced decisions at the CAA? You're admitting that.
Jason: I feel. I feel like you being you misunderstanding me …an influence can be positive. It can be negative. It can be done wrongly. Can be done in the right way.
55


The National Prosecuting Authority confirmed it’s preparing summons against Ken Roseveare and Sim Aero as well as Jason Maistry of the CAA, for extortion and conspiring against a competitor.

PAUSE
56


All of which could easily be dismissed as a disturbing - but isolated - spat between two competing businesses. Except, aviation rules require the CAA to have a firm hand across the board. What does it say about how it currently deals with the bigger players?
Last April SAA knowingly flew 184 passengers from Ghana to Joburg on a plane that had water-contaminated fuel in its tank. A highly unusual decision.


60
E.N-20230129_0001


COLIN JORDAAN: [00:11:22] fuel contamination is certainly one of the the big red flags for any operator. This aircraft departing from from Accra in Ghana. The aircraft itself, the previous day had detected that there was fuel contamination. It was when they were starting the engines, they got a warning to say fuel contamination.
61


The flight had been delayed… tanks drained… but without rigorous tests, it was impossible to be sure that contaminants were gone.
62
0749
GUY LEITCH: [00:06:02] They they should have flown that aircraft back empty as a ferry flight. Even so, it would have been risky for the crew and they were risking a whole lot.
63


GUY: [00:06:24] I think was a was an unacceptable risk in this situation to have loaded all full of passengers and cargo as well. Well, that really goes beyond any acceptable standard of safety.
64


On contaminated fuel, aviation history speaks for itself.
In 2008 a BA Boeing 777 crashed on landing at Heathrow…in 2010 Cathay Pacific nearly crashed in Hong Kong…
65


SAA admitted in a report to engine trouble mid-air on the flight from Ghana. and finding HIGH LEVELS of contaminants upon landing.
So..is it “all’s well that ends well”... just because THIS time no-one died?
66


We wanted answers from SAA, but they refused an interview.
67


The CAA also declined an interview, and even though they called us later to offer a written response, our inbox remains empty.
68




69
Day 2 Cam 1
P1644645


RICKY: [15:01:53] Unfortunately, there are elements in the CAA that are prepared to operate outside of what's right and wrong, and they will do whatever it takes to enrich themselves or to get a favor from somebody.
70

Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 05 February 2023 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Script: AIRTALES SCRIPT When a South African Airways Airbus A340-600 landed in Johannesburg from Accra, Ghana on 15 April last year, all was not as it seemed. During the flight, the plane’s engines started surging – an unusual occurrence for any aircraft as it may suggest contaminated fuel and demands urgent action from the flight crew. Alarmingly, though, the flight’s commander chose to continue flying back to O.R. Tambo International Airport… It was the third in a series of four recent incidents involving SAA. But, while other airlines have been grounded over safety concerns, the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) - mandated with regulating our airspace - has taken no action against the national carrier. Our probe uncovers evidence that all is not well at the CAA, undermining our country’s reputation for sterling air safety. Clip and Code Script 1 Setting foot on a plane, means putting your life in the hands of other PEOPLE… pilots, engineers, air traffic controllers and cabin crew… TO DATE South Africa had a reputation for safe air travel…our airspace tightly regulated…thanks to the Civil Aviation Authority. The CAA upholds a vast web of international laws and standards… …but could a number of incidents and the organisation’s own conduct over the last two years…raise questions over air safety? 2 Mike “Allen” Cam 1 C080 MIKE: [00:01:58] I think the CAA has become a political animal now. So consequently, as I say, it hears and it's guided by its political masters rather than its own, skill and the job it should be doing. 3 The CAA has rarely hesitated to act where it deemed safety was at stake. Cemair… Kulula… British Airways… and the maintenance company Lufthansa Technik …ALL GROUNDED in the last three years. 4 Links 0807 LINK: [17:38:31] South Africa's civil aviation authority flexes its muscles from time to time. But it seems at others, it turns a blind eye… are some airlines more equal than others? 5 Four incidents since 2021 might mean little in isolation.. but together…do they spell a dire warning? February 2021 - the national carrier South African Airways has a potentially disastrous safety incident on what we’ll call the BRUSSELS flight… April 2022 - a whistleblower leaks information that passengers were flown from Accra, Ghana to Joburg… in a plane with contaminated fuel.. and November 2022…an SAA plane bumper-bashes a Safair jet on the OR TAMBO airport apron. 6 Guy Leitch Day 1 Cam 1 0749 Guy Leitch is an aviation analyst and the editor of SA FLYER MAGAZINE UPSOUND: GUY [00:07:47] safety is a non-negotiable. Safety has to be taken for granted by the passengers. 7 Flying safely is all about preparation…about operating manuals and checklists and rigorous annual refresher training for the crew. Skipping a step …can be a problem. In February 2021 the government sent an SAA Airbus A340 600 to Belgium to collect Covid vaccines. SAA was in business rescue… air travel was in lockdown…the pilots needed refresher training. The CAA stopped SAA TWICE when not all the training was in place…but then, in an unusual move.. it waived some training requirements. 9 Colin Jordaan E.N-20230129_0001 For former SAA Pilot Colin Jordaan who headed up the CAA a decade ago the decision raised red flags. [00:08:12] it's difficult to understand what evidence could have been presented by the operator by, say, in order for this exemption to be granted. I certainly can't think of anything. 10 Without refresher training, pilots may not know that the Airbus A340 600 has a known computer glitch that is considered minor… if you know about it. If you don’t, it could kill you. On startup the plane’s computer SOMETIMES deducts around 80 tons from the weight data that the pilots capture manually… sudden weight loss impacts the plane’s ability to fly. 11 Mike 0807 Allen, not his real name, is a retired SAA pilot, who flew the A340-600 for a decade. [00:04:49] it's core to the whole aspect of a safe flight is knowing exactly how heavy your aircraft is….You're flying an aircraft that weighs 340 tons with 300 people or so. So you basically need to have those those factors and those figures are crucial and critical. 12 Several training documents and a cockpit checklist warn pilots about the glitch…In a report, SAA said those were not present on the Brussels flight which instead used an Airbus checklist that excluded the glitch. 13 COLIN JORDAAN E.N-20230129_0001 [00:16:08] I flew Airbus A340 600 from their inception. And that checklist was introduced exactly because this problem had occurred. 15 Moments into the flight, warnings sounded…the plane was about to stall.. Luckily the Airbus has a failsafe called the Alpha Floor system… 16 Mike “Allen” 0807 MIKE UPSOUND You could equate it almost to an ABS type of system on a motor car. It's to protect the aircraft from stalling. 17 The Alpha Floor saved the day… and potentially the lives of thousands of people on the ground. Had the CAA not waived the training requirement, it’s likely all this would have been avoided. 18 The plane landed in Brussels, loaded the vaccines and a day later headed off home. The pilots didn't tell anyone about the incident but the plane is designed to send a message to Airbus and engine manufacturer Rolls Royce. Incidents like this must be reported to the CAA within 72 hours. In fear of a near stall happening again, the pilots took off from on the return flight at a higher speed than European Union regulations allow - knowingly breaking an important law. 19 Mike Allen [00:16:25] the manually applied maximum thrust, which promptly had a aircraft behaving like a raging bull, if you like, and heading for the heavens at high speed. 20 Neither the pilots nor SAA said anything until a whistleblower leaked the information. 21 Link 0810 [17:47:09] SAA hasn't said much about the events which have unfolded, and they wouldn't speak to us saying they didn't want to get involved in a smear campaign. But it is unfair to expect transparency? 22 CAA ROR SAA presented a confidential incident report in Parliament a few weeks ago. The airline said.. the checklists that show the glitch have been put back.. 23 PAUSE AND TRANSITION TO RICKY But what the report didn’t say was that refresher training for pilots and crew could have prevented the whole debacle. 24 Meanwhile, within months of the Brussels flight, a local flight school owner would butt heads with the CAA in an incident which may at first seem like a personal spat. But, in the context of safety… it raises serious questions. Flight schools provide ongoing pilot training which the CAA licences and oversees. 25 Colin Jordaan E.N-20230129_0001 UPSOUND COLIN JORDAAN [00:09:11] Over the years, there have been a lot of instances where. Flying schools have used the CAA inspectors to achieve their own particular goals. 28 UPSOUND RICKIE [14:32:20] It's hugely competitive. It's very competitive. It's sometimes very cutthroat as well. 29 When Rickie Smit took over the reins at Sky Voyage in 2021 she had to apply for a new license… Owning a business was a big moment in her life…but on the sidelines, a competitor was plotting... 30 LINK It all started right here, at Denel’s Kempton Park Campus at the back of OR Tambo International Airport. This is where there is a simulator that Ricky uses. 31 … and when Ricky got a call from a prospective new client, she made a booking with THAT service provider. 32 But the call had come from a former client of a company called SimAero… which also has offices in the Denel complex 33 RICKY INTERVIEW [14:39:02] when I made a booking for a client to do training on. And on a simulator, not belonging to SimAero. I was called and told by SimAero staff that I'm stealing their clients. 34 DEREK [14:39:19] Were you? [14:39:19][0.3] 35 RICKY: [14:39:20] Absolutely not. There's no way I would steal anybody's clients 36 Calls and threats escalated -including from SimAero manager, Keith Roseveare… 37 RICKY: [14:41:16] I was bombarded with threats, but it all came through calls that I received. It was things like, if you don't give up the simulation to Simaero, you will be destroyed. I will make sure that you'll never operate again. We will have you shut down. We will make sure your operation will be completely demolished. There will be hell to pay 38 It turns out that SimAero tried to discredit her in any way possible. Eventually Roseveare reported Ricky for illegal training. His evidence: mock up training documents she used in preparation for a CAA audit that would have earned Sky Voyage its license. 39 Then Rickie got a call from a CAA Inspector who told her he was putting her licensing process on ice. But why would a company be shut down for dummy documents? Or was something else at play? PAUSE FOR DRAMA Coming up: From sweeping incidents under the carpet.. to shutting down industry entrepreneurs.. is this the role South Africans expect the CAA to play? ADBREAK 40 PART 2 INTRO The safety of our airspace depends on the Civil Aviation Authority policing the industry without fear or favour.. In part two we confront the inspector accused of shutting down a flight school at the behest of a competitor … and probe the infamous contaminated fuel flight. 41 TRANSITION BACK TO RICKY 42 Rickie Smit says a competitor threatened her for months, claiming a SimAero employee once relayed a disturbing message from his manager, Keith Roseveare - which Roseveare later denied. 43 Day 2 Cam 1 P1644645 RICKY : [14:42:06] He'll start by shooting my feet off and in my hands. And the only hell squeeze every blood cell out of my body until I'm left for dead. 44 45 Then, the CAA inspector Rickie relied on to help her through the trainer licensing process turned against her. 45 RICKY: I got a call from Jason Maestri And he told me that. He's calling me to tell me that he's cancelling the audit that was set for the next day to start. And the reason is that I acted fraudulently. I did illegal training. 46 Maistry shut Sky Voyage down… The CAA could never produce evidence of wrongdoing against Rickie - its own legal department exonerated her and told Maistry to issue her licence. But Maistry simply ignored the instruction. 49 DEREK: [15:00:10] Are you saying that the CAA was weaponised by a competitor? 50 RICKY: [15:00:15] Yes, they used Jason to weaponize themselves to achieve a goal so that they can take out another competitor out of the market 51 Keith Roseveare and Sim Aero did not want to talk to us… his attorneys sent court documents showing that he’s suing Ricky for defamation. The CAA wouldn’t be drawn on Rickie - saying in writing they have no knowledge of Rickie’s plight and asking us to give them our information. So we went straight to the source. 52 Day 2 Cam 1 P1644661 [16:38:11] is this Jason Maistry? JASON: YES DEREK: This is Derek from Carte Blanche. Jason Maistry talked in circles for a long time, trying to avoid speaking about Keith Roseveare. Eventually, he slipped up. 54 Jason Call [16:55:40] It came from the .. what is now opposition right, which was obviously from Keith. And because they had valid, valid evidence from the quality point of view or the quality management point of view. They found that, you know, a certain person was operating without a valid license. [16:56:08] But, Jason, this is what I've been asking you. And now you admitting that Keith Roseveare influenced decisions at the CAA? You're admitting that. Jason: I feel. I feel like you being you misunderstanding me …an influence can be positive. It can be negative. It can be done wrongly. Can be done in the right way. 55 The National Prosecuting Authority confirmed it’s preparing summons against Ken Roseveare and Sim Aero as well as Jason Maistry of the CAA, for extortion and conspiring against a competitor. PAUSE 56 All of which could easily be dismissed as a disturbing - but isolated - spat between two competing businesses. Except, aviation rules require the CAA to have a firm hand across the board. What does it say about how it currently deals with the bigger players? Last April SAA knowingly flew 184 passengers from Ghana to Joburg on a plane that had water-contaminated fuel in its tank. A highly unusual decision. 60 E.N-20230129_0001 COLIN JORDAAN: [00:11:22] fuel contamination is certainly one of the the big red flags for any operator. This aircraft departing from from Accra in Ghana. The aircraft itself, the previous day had detected that there was fuel contamination. It was when they were starting the engines, they got a warning to say fuel contamination. 61 The flight had been delayed… tanks drained… but without rigorous tests, it was impossible to be sure that contaminants were gone. 62 0749 GUY LEITCH: [00:06:02] They they should have flown that aircraft back empty as a ferry flight. Even so, it would have been risky for the crew and they were risking a whole lot. 63 GUY: [00:06:24] I think was a was an unacceptable risk in this situation to have loaded all full of passengers and cargo as well. Well, that really goes beyond any acceptable standard of safety. 64 On contaminated fuel, aviation history speaks for itself. In 2008 a BA Boeing 777 crashed on landing at Heathrow…in 2010 Cathay Pacific nearly crashed in Hong Kong… 65 SAA admitted in a report to engine trouble mid-air on the flight from Ghana. and finding HIGH LEVELS of contaminants upon landing. So..is it “all’s well that ends well”... just because THIS time no-one died? 66 We wanted answers from SAA, but they refused an interview. 67 The CAA also declined an interview, and even though they called us later to offer a written response, our inbox remains empty. 68 69 Day 2 Cam 1 P1644645 RICKY: [15:01:53] Unfortunately, there are elements in the CAA that are prepared to operate outside of what's right and wrong, and they will do whatever it takes to enrich themselves or to get a favor from somebody. 70

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): we question whether our skies are as safe as we are made to believe by our regulator, the Civil Aviation Authority
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Aviation fascinates audience, and this story introduces an element of significant tension as it will show the danger of corruption or sweeping investigations under the carpet can have devastating consequences. What are the dangers that lurk beneath the surface of shiny aircraft that fly us from A to B?
metadata.Further information: Are we safe when we fly? We look at 3 incidents that make us wonder whether we are as safe in the skies as we are led to believe. Firstly we look at training - and examine the case of Sim Aero, who seem to be up to dirty tricks in the industry in order to make more money. They have actively tried to put competitors out of business. But in doing so, our baddie Keith (the manager at Sim Aero) is about to be arrested for various nasty activities, including sexual harassment. But we look at his qualifications - he claims to be an examiner that can train and pass out pilots. But he is not. We have found at least one pilot that was signed out, illegally, by Keith and whose license leap frogged from a private license to piloting a twin engine passenger jet without any learning in between. And flying a commercial jet means this unqualified pilot is responsible for our lives. We confront Keith and the CAA inspector that we have on record (audio and affidavit from an investigator) that has taken bribes from Keith to destroy a competitor. The competitor, Ricky Smit from Sky Voyage, will narrate this ordeal for us. Then there is the curious case of SAA’s successful dodging of two incident investigations. We also look at 3 SAA incidents in the past 2 years that were never investigated. - the SAA Alpha Floor and noise abatement charges in Belgium. The crew who operated the flights did not complete their update training, it was waivered by the CAA in order to operate the flight- and the consequences could have been a crash over Joburg (Alpha Floor) It was the same commander in charge on both legs and there has never been an investigation into either incidents, as required by law, nor has SAA ever really answered the questions. Meanwhile, the commander was promoted to head of training. Meanwhile the same captain operated a flight on contaminated fuel from Ghana to Johannesburg - with more potential hazard for passengers. There were no consequences to either incident, it seems. And no investigation with an outcome by the CAA despite it being a dangerous and reportable event. ZA CARS - Joy did an insert, but we focus on the recent developments where the Ethiopian Accident Bureau investigation pointe to the CCA's complete lack of maintenance of the aircraft, the accident report said it was not airworthy, and how the Minister has now invalidated the enquiry. Reports swept under the carpet and brown envelopes, is this what our skies look like? There are some other operators who have an office, and not much else, yet they seem to be above the law. Malik of Cobra Air who has an AOC (Air Operator Certificate) but no aircraft - how does he pass inspections and how does he, along with FlyFofa, who are in the same position, manage to hang onto certification when they have nothing to certify? In addition, Keith from Sim Aero is about to be arrested on several charges. We will be there for the arrest. Planned confrontations: 1. Vox Pops (Malik, FlyFofa) 2. Keith at SIm Aero and his boss, Eric Renau 3. CAA 4. CAA official taking bribes (Jason Maistry) 5. SAA Interviews 1. Ricky 2. Aviation Expert 3. Airlines who are compliant (for balance)
